newsitem.title: INDIA: India sets 7.0 pct growth in 1997-2002 plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: India sets 7.0 pct growth in 1997-2002 plan - paper.

text.p: India will aim for an average annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate of 7.0 percent in its next five-year economic plan scheduled to begin on April 1, 1997, Business Standard said on Wednesday.

The newspaper reported that the government said in its approach paper for the Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002) that it planned to step up GDP growth, which averaged 5.9 percent in the Eighth Plan (1992-97), by stimulating savings and efficiency.

The approach paper, which outlines the broad strategy of economic planning based on government spending and investment policies, was approved by the Indian cabinet earlier this week, the newspaper said.
In the Ninth Plan, the government plans a domestic savings rate of 26.2 percent compared with 23.7 percent in the Eighth Plan, it said.

The incremental capital-output ratio (ICOR) which measures the number of units of capital required to produce one unit of output, is expected to come down to 4.08 in the Ninth Plan from 4.24 in the Eighth Plan, the newspaper said.
A lower ICOR indicates higher economic efficiency.
The Ninth Plan strategy envisages an annual average export growth of 14.5 percent, as against 11.4 percent in the Eighth Plan that ends on March 31, 1997, the newspaper said.
Imports are expected to grow at an average annual rate of 15.3 percent as against 13.6 percent in the Eighth Plan, it said.

The government also envisages higher foreign investment helped by a proposed rise in the percentage of equity foreign firms can hold with automatic government approval in Indian companies to 74 percent from the current 51 percent, it said.
The government plans to lift state control in the form of licences required for manufacture in the coal and sugar industries, it said.
The economic plans are made by the government's Planning Commission.
